definitions.explanation: A large Japanese dog breed originally from Akita Prefecture, with a curled tail and thick double coat. Famous worldwide through Hachikō, the loyal Shibuya dog.

examples.japanese: {秋田犬|あきたいぬ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飼|か}っている→飼う：08151_kau⟧。
{秋田犬|あきたいぬ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{忠実|ちゅうじつ}→忠実：12570_chuujitsu⟧な⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: Akitas are known for their loyal personality.

examples.japanese: ⟦{渋谷|しぶや}→渋谷：30632_shibuya⟧⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な⟦{銅像|どうぞう}→銅像：14471_douzou⟧ハチ{公|こう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{秋田犬|あきたいぬ}だ。
examples.english: The famous statue Hachikō at Shibuya Station is an Akita.

notes:
Also read あきたけん in everyday speech; the あきたいぬ reading is preferred by breed associations. Named after Akita Prefecture in northern Japan, where the breed was developed.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {秋田犬|あきたいぬ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飼|か}う→飼う：08151_kau⟧: to own an Akita
- {純血|じゅんけつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{秋田犬|あきたいぬ}: a purebred Akita
- {大型犬|おおがたけん}: large-breed dog (category Akita falls in)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Designated a natural treasure (⟦{天然記念物|てんねんきねんぶつ}→天然記念物：04899_tennenkinenbutsu⟧) in 1931. Hachikō, the Akita who waited daily at Shibuya Station for his deceased owner, is a national symbol of loyalty, and Akitas have also been given as gifts to foreign dignitaries including Helen Keller and Russian president Vladimir Putin.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{柴犬|しばいぬ}→柴犬：27503_shibainu⟧: Shiba Inu — smaller Japanese breed; both belong to the {日本犬|にほんけん} (Japanese dog) group
